So what we do is do more evil to ignore the fact that we cannot forgive ourselves. Does that make sense? So evil creates more evil. Evil compounds on evil. So now we're just stuck.

The garden of Eden is metaphorical. We left the garden of Eden not because we broke the law, but because we cannot forgive ourselves from the evil that we've committed and so we keep on doing more and more evil.

Okay. The first possibility is to compensate for the first act of disobedience, but you can't do that because you try to be God. You try to kill God. So you cannot ever compensate God for the evil you've done.

The other possibility is that God forgives you. But if God just forgives you, you won't learn anything. Man in his limits could not recompense for no obedience, no humility he offered later could have been so deep that it could match the heights he made to reach through disobedience. Man lacked the power to offer satisfaction by himself.

For God show greater generosity in giving his own self that man might be able to rise than if he simply pardoned. For every other means fell short of justice except the way whereby the son of God humbled himself, becoming incarnate. Incarnate just means human. So this is why Jesus had to kill himself.

The analogy is this: I'm a father and I have a daughter named Eve, and I have a dog. I say to Eve, "I love you, Eve, so much." And then Eve says to me, "Do you love me or do you love the dog more?" I said, "I love you both equally." Of course, I love you, but I also love the dog. And Eve goes and kills the dog.

Eve says to me, "Hey, do you love me or do you love the dog more?" Now I'm stuck because if I punish her, that shows her I love the dog more. But if I don't punish her, she's going to kill another animal. So what do I do? God decides to punish himself so that we would be humbled by a sacrifice. We would feel so much regret and remorse for making God die that we would never disobey him again.

God had to punish himself so that we would be humbled by a sacrifice, feeling so much regret and remorse for making God die, ensuring we would never try to become God ourselves. This is why Jesus freed us from the evil in us and led us to the path of good. Now all we have to do is remember Jesus, remember what he said, and forever be on the path towards the light.

Uh, do I completely make it up or just forgive myself because I think I can't?
